relations.subject: Ahmad Hasan Dani
relations.evidence: He graduated in 1944 with an MA degree in Sanskrit, becoming the first Muslim graduate of Banaras Hindu University.

relations.subject: Ahmad Hasan Dani
relations.evidence: In 1945, he started working as a trainee in archaeology under the guidance of Mortimer Wheeler.

relations.subject: Ahmad Hasan Dani
relations.evidence: For a period of twelve years (between 1950 and 1962), Dani remained associate professor of history at University of Dhaka

relations.subject: Ahmad Hasan Dani
relations.object: School of Oriental and African Studies, University of London
relations.evidence: During his associate professorship at Dhaka University, Dani worked as a research fellow at the School of Oriental and African Studies, University of London (1958–59).

relations.subject: Ahmad Hasan Dani
relations.evidence: Dani moved to the University of Peshawar in 1962, where he established the Department of Archaeology, and remained a professor until 1971.

relations.subject: Ahmad Hasan Dani
relations.evidence: Later, in 1969 he became Asian Fellow at the Australian National University, Canberra.

relations.subject: Ahmad Hasan Dani
relations.role: dean of Faculty of Social Sciences
relations.evidence: In 1971, he moved to University of Islamabad to become dean of Faculty of Social Sciences. He left the post in 1975 to concentrate on research as professor of history.

relations.subject: Ahmad Hasan Dani
relations.evidence: In 1974, he went to the University of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia as a visiting scholar.

relations.subject: Ahmad Hasan Dani
relations.evidence: In 1977, he was a visiting professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison.

relations.subject: Ahmad Hasan Dani
relations.evidence: In 1997, Dani became an honorary director at the Taxila Institute of Asian Civilizations. He held the position until the time of his death.

relations.subject: Ahmad Hasan Dani
relations.evidence: From 1985, he was involved in research focusing on the documentation of the rock carvings and inscriptions... along with Harald Hauptmann of Heidelberg Academy of Sciences, University of Heidelberg.
